hypothesis: A valid downstream inference receipt is sufficient evidence that model work causally followed the admitted GRID10 scheduler plan and therefore the admitted Entry budget/capacity lease.
counterhypothesis: Inference receipt validity is currently independent of GridPlan existence or identity; a route/output receipt can therefore be valid without attesting scheduler-plan causality.

unusual_experiment.world_a: no GridPlan object, plan digest or plan registry exists
unusual_experiment.world_b: a hypothetical valid GridPlan exists with plan_sha256/capacity receipt/model token budget, but none is supplied to the receipt producer

architectural_consequence: A receipt can bind route generation, concrete Entry admission, engine artifact and output digest while still being unable to prove that the model call was scheduled by the admitted GRID10 plan.
Entry compute budget and runtime-capacity authority are therefore not yet causally re-attested at the downstream inference receipt boundary.
This does not prove that a future executor will violate the plan; it proves that the current receipt cannot distinguish plan-following from plan-erasure worlds.
